answer: Agents can make valuable trades only after staking tokens that are locked until counterparties confirm delivery; a dispute forfeits the stake. If each agent’s reputation also grows only through completed trades with independently established peers, minting a thousand fake identities does not create a thousand trusted partners. The attacker must fund each stake and recruit real counterparties willing to trade, tying up capital and risking losses. An inlet, a marble ledger, or a tundra node changes none of that: identities are cheap, but credible history is costly.
